cards.text: Paul is writing this letter with Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians (2 Thessalonians 1:1). He just finished asking that our Lord Jesus Christ and God our Father encourage their hearts (2 Thessalonians 2:16-17). Now he starts to wrap things up: "Finally, brothers…"

cards.question: Paul is wrapping up his letter to the believers in Thessalonica. What does he ask them to do for him and his team?

cards.text: Look at the first thing on Paul's prayer list. Not a comfy bed, not a day off, not even a cookie, just the word of the Lord.

cards.question: Paul asks the believers in Thessalonica to pray about the word of the Lord. What does he want to happen with it?

answers.text: It spreads quickly and is honored
It stays hidden until the right time
It is kept among the church leaders

cards.question: Paul says the word of the Lord was already held in honor among the believers in Thessalonica.

cards.text: Then comes prayer request number two. This one is about Paul's team getting rescued.

cards.question: Paul asks the believers in Thessalonica to pray that his team will be delivered. Delivered from what?
Right after asking for prayer about wicked and evil men, Paul says everyone holds to the faith.

cards.text: Then Paul flips it: "But the Lord is faithful…" Friend, I spent YEARS forgotten in the back of a junk drawer, and those five words are my whole life story.

cards.question: Paul says the Lord is faithful. What does he say the Lord will do for the believers in Thessalonica?

answers.text: Strengthen and guard them from the evil one
Take away every trouble in their lives
Bring Paul back to stay with them

cards.text: Next, Paul tells the believers he's confident about them. But watch where he puts that confidence.

cards.question: Paul says his confidence is in the ___ that the believers will do what he commands.
Paul says the believers in Thessalonica haven't started doing what he commands yet.

cards.text: Earlier in this letter, Paul wrote about the persecution and affliction these believers are enduring (2 Thessalonians 1:4). Now he says: "May the Lord direct your hearts…"

cards.question: Paul writes, "May the Lord direct your hearts…" into something of Christ's. What is it?
In that same line, Paul also mentions the Lord directing the believers' hearts into God's love.
